articleTitle: Synchrophasor Data Based Distributed Droop Control in Grid Integrated Wind Farms to Improve Primary Frequency Response
abstract: In power system, the wind power generation is gradually increasing to encourage the sustainable growth of electricity production, resulting shut down of fossil fuel based conventional plants. Due to this, system inertia reduces which degrades stability of the grid. To overcome the situation, interest is on droop control mechanism for the wind turbines (WT). This paper proposes a synchrophasor data based distributed droop control (SDDC) for the grid integrated wind farms (WFs), to improve primary frequency response (PFR) of power system. The method uses phasor measurement unit (PMU) data to obtain load-generation mismatch in the power system. Thereby, ratio of power reserve (RPR) is calculated for the WFs. The RPRs are based on power reserve (PR) and installed capacity of the WFs. The RPR is further used to obtain power share for each WT, based on their wind speed, inside the respective WF. The power share is used to calculate required change in droop at the WTs to generate the allocated share. The performance of the proposed SDDC is verified for a load disturbance, variation in wind speed at a WF and a synchronous generator outage. In these situations, the proposed method is found to be more effective, as compared to the available distributed Newton (DN) method.

articleTitle: Assessing the impacts of integration of Solar PV on transient stability of the power system using a sensitivity based index
abstract: Study on the impact of penetration of renewable energy sources on power system stability is a present day need. The impact of huge penetration of PV system on transient stability condition of multi-machine power system is discussed in this paper. The application of trajectory sensitivity analysis in estimating the stability of the whole system integrated with solar PV is discussed here. A new index which is based on sensitivity of the terminal voltage of Solar PV farm is proposed that can assess the system stability condition for constant and as well as varying penetration levels. With the help of this index a suitable location for PV in an existing power system may be obtained and also the proposed index indicates the relative stability condition for increase in solar PV power penetration. The study has been done in a WSCC 3-machine 9-bus system in MATLAB platform.

articleTitle: Development of Feed-In-Tariff using Unbundle Smart Meters for Small Scale Wind Power Generating Plant and Small-Scale Roof-Top Solar Plant
abstract: With developing demands for alternative energy sources, large number of wind power generating farms and solar power plant are getting deployed throughout the world. Small home-based wind turbines and solar generator are also gaining popularity as Prosumers are increasing in current smart grid scenario. Going with the current trends, Feed-In-Tariff (FiT) concept and Net Energy metering could provide solution for efficient integration of wind energy to grid. In this paper two case studies have been presented of FiT for a small wind farm a n d a small roof-top solar plant, feeding power to central grid. The FiT has been developed in unbundled smart meter (USM) as it provides the flexibility to add new features to the meter. The microcontroller based smart meter is programmed with feature for data acquisition of power generated from a small- scale wind turbine and roof-top solar plant. This data is used for case studying the effect of FiT for energy billing optimization and hence promoting the growth of renewable to grid integration.

articleTitle: Reliability Test of Restructured Power System with Capacity Expansion and Transmission Switching
abstract: The time duration required to design, construct and commission a large generating station can be quite extensive depending upon the environmental and regulatory requirements. So it becomes a necessary part to examine the future load demand and solution to serve the demand. Capacity expansion analysis is one of the major solutions for reducing the system risk level and serving the future load demand. This paper discusses about the system reliability performance improvement with capacity expansion of restructured power system. Peak load carrying capability (PLCC) can be observed with different unavailability of generating units and with addition of new generating units in the system. Reliability indices such as LOLE or risk level, EDNS, EENS and DPUI are examine with capacity expansion and transmission switching in different peak load conditions. Effect of maintenance of generating units have been also observed in terms of risk level and reliability performance.

articleTitle: A Non-iterative Three Phase Distribution System Power Flow Analysis
abstract: A novel non-iterative three phase power flow has been proposed in this paper for distribution systems. Due to high R/X ratio and unbalance in load of distribution systems, the linear DC power flow is not applicable as resistance can’t be neglected. Moreover, voltage magnitudes play vital role in distribution systems. So, the aim of this paper is to develop a linear power flow for unbalanced distribution system which takes into account of both resistance and voltage magnitude along with reactance and voltage angle unlike DC power flow. The proposed method is implemented and tested on 19-bus, and 25- bus unbalanced radial distribution systems and is bench marked against standard backward forward sweep power flow analysis. Though the method is developed for unbalanced radial distribution systems, it is still valid for weakly mesh connected system as well.

articleTitle: A Method to Predict Degree of Polymerization Value of Oil-paper Insulation Using Interfacial Charge
abstract: Analysis based on Degree of Polymerization (DP) value is assumed to provide reliable regarding insulation condition. However, due to the invasive nature of testing, DP value based-analysis is not feasible in practical cases as it requires a paper sample from the in-service unit. Here, an attempt is made to develop a methodology to predict DP value based on non-invasive testing of oil-paper insulation. In this paper, it is found that DP value maintains a well-known relation with interfacial charge (estimated using Polarization Depolarization Current data) as both these parameters are related to the cellulosic condition. The proposed method successfully applied on various laboratory prepared samples containing different moisture content.

articleTitle: CAN-based architecture for MSC-GCCI with Maximum Power Point Tracking in large PV installations
abstract: This paper presents a novel CAN protocol based Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) for the Master-slave Configured Grid-connected Centralized Inverters (MSCGCCI) in large solar power plants. The CAN protocol is a multi-master and has a very high immunity towards EMI/EMC issues arisen due to switching of the devices in power electronics converters. The proposed CAN protocol is reliable, deterministic and can go up to the maximum signaling speed of 1M bits per second. The CAN-based communication is ideally suited for power electronics application particularly for MSC-GCCI based architecture where each of the parallelconnected inverters communicates its online status and other critical information to the master inverter. In the case of the CAN communication failure, the proposed CAN protocol ensures that the total power from the slave inverter doesn't go to zero. The proposed MPPT algorithm along with CAN-based communication is implemented in 2 × 25 kW hardware set-up. The static and dynamic MPPT efficiency of the MSC-GCCI is tested as per EN50530 standard.

articleTitle: Modeling and Detection of Inter-turn Faults in Distribution Transformer
abstract: In a Distribution system, transformer is one of the major equipment, which are vulnerable to various kinds of faults. Amongst all, internal winding faults are most severe. Generally, transformer protection is done by differential protection scheme. Upon an internal fault, the rise in current is comparatively less for incipient faults or shorted turns less than 10% of total turns, and may not be enough to operate a differential over current relay. As these internal winding faults are severe, it leads to complete damage of transformer and consequently shutdown of the distribution system. Practical experimental analysis is not possible for the distribution transformer internal winding faults, as, due to the experiment, the transformer may get completely damaged. Therefore, these kinds of analysis are generally done using software simulations. So far, most of the analysis on transformer internal winding faults are done by using EMTP simulations. In this work, the equivalent circuit of transformer is considered and transformer is modelled using equations. In this proposed model primary voltages are given as inputs, secondary currents are outputs and primary as well as secondary side flux equations are internal variables. The inter turn faults of distribution transformer are modelled and simulated using MATLAB/SIMULINK tool. The modelling of transformers inter turn fault is done with the help of equations and the results obtained validate the model presented.

articleTitle: Practical Approaches Towards Securing Edge Devices in Smart Grid
abstract: Security is a big concern in the adaptation of edge computing for smart grid technologies. As the processing power and capabilities of Intelligent Electronic Devices (IEDs) in the power grid increases, they also become prime targets for attackers to exploit for their own gain. Utilities are especially concerned with distribution systems, as the IEDs may not use dedicated fibre communications. It is no longer sufficient to use a single method to secure an IED; using multiple methods can increase the difficulty for an attacker to be covert and may detect malicious behaviour faster. This paper describes some techniques that are currently being implemented on a custom built multifunctional IED using a credit card sized supercomputer called Parallella. An implementation of a remote attestation scheme based on process memory is discussed. An approach to detect malicious device behaviour using osquery, a free and open source tool is also discussed. Finally, network booting and how it is used it to ease updating or resetting devices in the field is elaborated.

articleTitle: Demand side management through Hydro URS in North-Eastern Region
abstract: NER grid faces the issue of high unpredictable generation during the `peak-hydro' season throughout monsoon due to generation mix being in favour of hydro power. Major hydro plants in NER are Run-of-River (ROR) Plants with limited storage. ROR plants are must-run generating stations and sudden rainfall increases the water flow to create a huge surplus of power in the region. It is a challenge on the part of a state/beneficiary to carry out proper load forecasting for its control area. The unpredictable weather conditions make it difficult to maintain the balance between generation and demand. A mechanism is being proposed through this paper that will help the beneficiaries/ state for better real-time load-generation balancing.

articleTitle: Reduced-Scale Wide Area Control System Design Based Upon the Dominancy Index Analysis
abstract: The objective of this paper is to develop an efficient wide area control (WAC) system with minimum possible involvement of system-wide entities. The wide area control signals are generated for generators' excitation systems. The state feedback control technique is employed. In the conventional approach, the WAC system is realized by involving all the generators in the WAC loop. This may requires a large communication network infrastructure increasing both the cost and complexity of the WAC system. In contrast, the approach that is employed in this paper is based upon the identification of generators that are primarily responsible for causing the inter-area oscillations. Thus, instead of providing wide area control signals to all the generators, those are generated only for the dominant generators in inter-area oscillatory modes. Furthermore, only the states of dominant generators are considered for generating WAC signals. The H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>-norm optimization technique with structural constraints is employed to get the required state feedback gain matrix. The effectiveness of the proposed WAC system is verified by considering different case studies through off-line simulations.

articleTitle: Fault detection in MTDC network utilising one end measurements
abstract: The voltage source converter (VSC) based Multi-Terminal Direct Current (MTDC) system is used to transfer the bulk amount of power over large distances by connecting two or more AC/DC converter stations. However, the exposure of the MTDC transmission network to various atmospheric conditions paralleled with the vulnerability of semiconductor devices in VSCs leads to a high chance of failure and fault. This fault, if persists for a long time will result into total shutdown of the network. To avoid this condition, it is important to detect the fault in the MTDC network in the least possible time. Thus, the present paper introduces a novel approach using the Fuzzy Inference System (FIS) for detecting the fault in VSC based MTDC transmission lines. The fault is created at different locations of the transmission line to study the performance of the presented method. The presented strategy provides the benefit of 98.6% reach setting of relay and rapid fault detection. The performance and effectiveness of implemented FIS based approach for fault detection is studied and verified in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Notice of Retraction: Gauss/Mouse Map based Chaotic Lightning Search Algorithm for Sizing and Allocation of DG and DSTATCOM Considering Probabilistic Load Flow
abstract: Retracted.

articleTitle: Operational Management of Grid Connected Microgrid with Responsive Loads
abstract: In this work operational management of the grid connected AC microgrid with renewables and responsive loads is presented. The operational problem is formulated by combining two different functions; total consumption cost and total operating cost of the prosumer driven microgrid. A new operational model with Demand Side Management (DSM) is proposed to manage the responsive loads in microgrid. A multib-objective problem is formulated for the proposed model and different operational cases with and without DSM are considered. The problem is solved by implementing combined Particle Swarm Optimization and Technique for Order of Preferences by Similarity to Ideal Solution(PSO-TOPSIS). Results are compared for the considered operational cases and found to be encouraging.

articleTitle: Online Voltage Stability Assessment using Wide Area Measurements
abstract: Loads and operating conditions continuously undergo changes in a power system. Changes in load are arbitrary in nature and the load power factor may or may not remain constant. Load change affects the voltage profile of the system. Excessive change in load may lead to voltage instability in the system and a proper indication is required to confirm how far the system is from impending instability through the usage of voltage stability indices. Available voltage instability identification methods, depending on rate of voltage variation with respect to active/reactive load power changes, are valid only for variations in active/reactive load or for load variations with constant power factor. An index for assessing voltage stability has been proposed here. It is valid for any type of load variations with variable power factor. The method, proposed in this paper, is implemented on New England 39 bus system and North Eastern grid of India consisting of 233 buses. Results demonstrate the accuracy of the method.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling for Residential Building Based on Virtual Energy Storage System
abstract: The virtual energy storage system (VESS) achieved by using the demand response of thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) is becoming more popular for smart grid. Demand response of TCLs to provide a cost-effective solution in real-time for the power mismatch due to variable renewable energy generation and avoid extra expenses due to meet the peak demand. To extract energy-saving and lesser cost of electricity, residential consumers perform energy management in accordance with power by grid, renewable generation, energy storage, demand response of TCLs, and electricity price. This requires optimal scheduling of residential consumer demand with manage the energy consumption of TCLs for cost saving. Firstly, mathematical model of TCLs and VESS using TCLs are developed. Then, an optimal scheduling model is developed to minimize the electricity cost of residential consumers. The simulations results show the reduction in the cost of electricity and VESS provides services like conventional energy storage.

articleTitle: Dynamic State Estimation of Synchronous Generator based Distributed Energy Resource in Autonomous Microgrid
abstract: The reliability and security of microgrid vastly depends on the fast control actions. Synchronous generator based Distributed Energy Resources (DER) are mostly commissioned in microgrid because of low cost and easy to control. When the microgrid toggle from grid connected mode to islanded mode, the control of DER is crucial to support the critical loads without compromising on reliability. A robust dynamic state estimator (DSE) can be employed to get an access to internal states of the generator for control. With the advent of //PMU into the distribution system made DSE possible. Due to the uncertainty of renewable energy resources and loads, DSE plays a vital role in monitoring and control applications. The real time monitoring of internal states of synchronous generator based DER is achieved by using kalman filter variants have been implemented in DSE. In this paper linearized variant and non-linear variants of kalman filter such as extended kalman filter (EKF), Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF), Square-root Unscented Kalman filter (SRUKF) and Robust Unscented kalman filter (RUKF) respectively have been implemented and tested for DSE. SRUKF and RUKF gives best estimates to the states with less absolute error when compared to other techniques. Computation time of RUKF is way less than SRUKF, hence RUKF is better alternative to SRUKF for real time DSE in microgrids.

articleTitle: Stability of DC Microgrid for Different Reduced Communication Topologies
abstract: Distributed secondary controllers for dc microgrid require information exchange between the sources. The information exchange is achieved by either a full communication or a reduced communication topology. Using consensus control, a good performance can be achieved in dc microgrid with reduced communication. However, the effects of communication topology on system stability is not analyzed in detail in literature. For a given power network, various reduced communication topologies are possible. The stability of system depends on communication network topology and the power network parameters. This paper investigates stability of dc microgrid for different communication topologies. Equations for the system with the secondary controller using reduced communication is derived and state space model is analyzed to see the effect of communication topology on the stability of the system. Results are validated through MATLAB/Simulink based simulations.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of μPMU Placement for Active Distribution Network’s Observability
abstract: Various Optimal PMU Placement (OPP) formulation have been proposed in the literature for topological observability of a power transmission system. This paper assesses the suitability of such methods for the placement of Distribution-Level Phasor Measurement Units (known as D-PMUs or μPMUs) in the active distribution network (ADN). The various OPP models such as cost minimization, channel limitation, effect of zero injection buses, single PMU loss, single line outage, multistage placement, maximization of measurement redundancy are framed and solved using Integer Linear Programming (ILP) for various ADNs such as, IEEE 33, 69 and 123 bus system. The ratio of the number of buses and μ-PMUs, system measurement redundancy, depth of unobservability are considered as performance indices to compare various OPP solutions in case of normal operation, network reconfiguration and island formation.

articleTitle: Selective Eigenvalue Analysis for Wide-Area Measurement and Control Applications – A Review
abstract: Selective eigenvalue analysis of linearised power system models is a well-known analysis technique in power system studies. Wide area measurement systems have made available online estimates of the critically damped modes in power systems. While wide area actuators in the form of power electronics actuators (HVDC, FACTS, renewable actuators) have provided additional flexibility in control of these oscillations. These actuators have lead to the need for further adaptations to selective eigen analysis tools. This paper presents a review of selective eigen analysis tools used in power system studies and brings out newer requirements in the context of wide area measurements and control.

articleTitle: Cyber Attack Detection In Smart Grid Substation Using Virtual Range Increment And Trust Weight
abstract: In power system protection, the protective zones overlap each other making it difficult to understand which relay or circuit breaker should operate first. Similarly, in smart grid substations different Wireless Sensors (WS) are used for data exchange and communication, whose area of operation overlap each other. During a cyber intrusion, it is difficult to identify the actual defected or compromised sensors. Cyber intrusion in WS spoofing their location, identity, and data. This paper proposes an approach for resolving cyber intrusion detection in the overlapped area of smart grid substation sensors. Each sensor is denoted by a graph node with a circle enclosing the node showing its communication range. Though to detect the malicious nodes during cyber intrusion the traditional trust weight method is used in combination with Virtual Range Increment (VRI). Each sensor node detects the weighs value of the surrounding adjacent node, compare with the threshold weight value. With the help of the trust weight method different suspicious nodes are identified. By using VRI the working area of sensor nodes is increased virtual using MATLAB so that the exact malicious nodes can be identified from suspicious nodes. The proposed method also reduces the time of detection making Smart Grid Substation (SGS) less vulnerable to cyber intrusion.

articleTitle: Analysis of Higher Partial Discharge Values in 36 kV Resin Cast Epoxy Bushings: A Case Study
abstract: After studying almost 20 years in past operational data, it was found that partial discharge leading to insulation failure in resin epoxy cast bushings is very frequent. The main cause for these failures is bad design which lead to high electrical stress causing insulation breakdown. Flaws in the manufacturing process under the influence of continuous operation cause insulation failure. Severe operating environment in the field lead to catastrophic failure. In this paper, to understand the root cause of above problems special techniques are discussed including simulation using 3D Electric Field Modelling by Finite Element Method. A case study is showcased where dissection analysis on bushings was implemented on the bushings having high PD values. Finally, partial discharge test on full scale prototypes are validated with 3D field computation results.

articleTitle: Droop based DG allocation in weakly meshed autonomous microgrid
abstract: The rising renewable based power penetration in the conventional distribution systems have popularized the concept of autonomous microgrids. However, frequency (f) and voltage (V) deviations are major concern due to intermittency of load and renewable generations. The droop based DGs can supply the growing load but require an optimal placement and an optimal droop coefficient so that their allocation does not cause f and V deviations beyond standard limits. In the present work, optimal droop-based DGs placement and its corresponding optimal droop coefficient calculation has been done to supply rising loads considering minimization of f and V deviations. The analysis has been conducted on standard IEEE-33 weakly meshed distribution network which has been modified as autonomous microgrid. The results have been obtained for various load levels and valuable conclusions have been drawn in the end.

articleTitle: Small signal stability analysis of wind farm integrated multi-machine power system with distributed load
abstract: Wind energy is one of the fastest growing energy resources of alternative power generation across the globe. Maximum number of generators in wind farm is provided with Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) due to its many advantages. The effects on small signal stability of system with distributed additional load, equipped with DFIG based wind farms, is presented here. The additional load added in the existing system is made same in value as the power generated by the wind farm. Different distributions of additional load are considered to determine the small signal stability of system with varying wind power penetration. The position of the negative real part of eigenvalues of system matrix helps to determine the best location for the integration of wind power for particular load distribution of additional load among different load buses. A new sensitivity based index has been introduced here to determine the maximum penetration level in terms of the system small signal stability. WSCC 3-machine 9-bus system is used for the study which is carried out in MATLAB.

articleTitle: Unscented Kalman Filter based Mechanical Parameter Estimation of Wind Power Systems
abstract: A variable speed wind power generation system consists a number of controllers. The design of these controllers needs true information of the system parameters for their coordinated control. However, sometimes the exact parameters of the system may not be present which may result the malfunctioning of the employed controllers. Further, the parameters also change with the time and it may also be a reason of mal-operation of the controllers. Thus, there is a need of estimation of the system parameters which gives the exact information of the system parameters and accordingly the operator can update the controller to prevent the mal-functioning. The objective of this work includes online estimation of various mechanical parameters, especially stiffness coefficient and damping constant of the turbine-generator coupling shaft, since the information of the electrical parameters can be found by various simplified tests. Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) has been used for parameter-estimation with the help of terminal measurements which include generator speed, active and reactive power. The DFIG based wind power generation scheme is used for the study wherein the estimation of the parameters has been performed in various wind speed environments.

articleTitle: Power Displacement Analysis for Power Systems - A Commodity Model
abstract: Power is a commodity that is said to be delivered by displacement in power systems. It is like an ice-baton passed by one runner to another in a relay race, with some loss at each transfer. Mathematical analysis of this physical view is presented in this paper. An innovative concept of junction in place of bus is proposed for this purpose. At junctions, power-displacements are specified. Computation is first done for one-generator modules. Superposition of results from modules is used for multi-generator case. Generators push powers towards the load because of turbines behind them. In this process they push one another. Mathematical analysis of this mechanism is used to obtain line-flows, voltages, their phase-angles and reactive powers of generators. NR-flow is not needed. Regions of influence of generators can also be determined. This commodity model is expected to be useful for regulators dealing with power markets.

articleTitle: Voltage Control in Active Distribution Networks and an Approach based on Model Predictive Control
abstract: With the rise in penetration of renewable energy sources in electric distribution networks, reliable operation and control of power system have become a challenge for power system operators. The paradigm shift from passive to active distribution network causes various issues such as, stability, voltage and frequency regulation, designing of protection equipment, etc. Thus, there arises the need of a proper control strategy to deal with such concerns. This paper presents a review of the voltage control strategies already existed in literature. Subsequently, a methodology is also proposed here to regulate voltages in active distribution networks.

articleTitle: Hierarchical Coordinated Control of Electric Vehicle Parking Lot in Distribution System
abstract: Uncoordinated charging of EVs may result in overloading, increased losses and voltage deviations in distribution system. In this context, coordinated charging of EVs by parking lot operator (PLO) is a potential solution these problems. PLO coordinates charging of EVs during low electricity prices to avail monitory benefits. However, charging of EVs during low electricity prices results in unusual peaks which may adversely affect the operation of distribution system. Therefore, coordinated scheduling of EVs by PLO considering operational constraints of distribution system is essential. To this end, this study proposes a hierarchical framework of coordination between PLO and distribution system operator (DSO) for scheduling of EVs. In the hierarchy, PLO coordinates the charging demand of EVs to minimizing the charging cost. Thereafter, optimal operation of distribution system is considered at DSO level with EVs load demand obtained from PLO. If the operational constraints of distribution system are violated, DSO determines the load boundaries for EVs load and communicates to PLO. Finally, PLO allocates the charging demand to EVs considering the load boundaries suggested by DSO. The proposed methodology is validated on 33-bus radial distribution system. Simulation results indicate that proposed approach results in efficient operation of distribution system while minimizing charging cost to PLO.

articleTitle: Wavelet Transform Modulus Maxima-based Fault Location Method for Three-Terminal Transmission Line
abstract: This paper introduced a new wavelet transform modulus maxima-based fault distance method for three-terminal transmission lines. The presented method decouples the phase currents using Clark's transformation. Then, the modulus maxima of the wavelet transform (WTMM) signal is calculated for the identification of the arrival of traveling waves. The proposed method uses WTMM corresponding to an aerial and zero-mode component of traveling wave to identify the correct faulty line section. The next task of fault distance calculation is carried out using a single-ended traveling wave method. The proposed method requires the current data measured un/synchronized at all the terminals of transmission line. This method is applicable to ground faults only. The method remains valid even for faults which are very close to the terminal and junction point of three line-section. The authenticity of this scheme is evaluated by simulating different scenarios with the frequency-dependent line model of the three-terminal transmission line in a software EMTDC/PSCAD. The results indicate a good level of accuracy for the proposed fault location method.

articleTitle: Network Constraint Compliant Choice of Renewable Energy Source Sitting
abstract: The renewable energy sources are being incorporated into the existing power system for a clean, cheap and feasible source of power generation. The system operator must inspect that the sites allocated for incorporating renewable energy sources (RES) can provide maximum utilization of RES. The paper proposes an approach to find out the suitable sites for integrating RES on the basis of maximum power that can be injected at these sites without violating transmission network constraints. The approach leads to the identification of the best and the worst sites or buses on the basis of transmission constraints. Furthermore, the paper gives an idea about the nature of the different buses in response to RES incorporation. It depicts the maximum quantum of the power that can be integrated on each bus without violating the power flow limits of any transmission line. It identifies the transmission lines that are the cause of concern for integrating RES. The proposal is demonstrated on IEEE 30 bus and IEEE 118 bus systems.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Pricing to Mitigate Uncertain Load Scenario
abstract: Distribution network pricing approaches produces forward looking, economically efficient, and locational pricing signal to users. Such approaches assume a fixed load growth rate in all future scenarios, which is practically not possible. Uncertain load growth rate may cause the asset capacity's full utilization before the reinforcement time period. So, from the reliability perspective some asset capacity needs to be reserved. In this paper LRIC pricing model has been enhanced to accommodate the uncertain load growth. Minimum allowable reserve capacity (MARC) has been incorporated in basic LRIC model to cope up the risk of uncertain load growth rate. The proposed pricing approach is demonstrated on a 22-bus practical Indian reference network. Results from proposed approach are validated with basic LRIC approach.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Very Fast Transient Over-voltages in 400 kV GIS
abstract: Power systems is subjected to various forms of transient phenomena's realized essentially by the sudden variations in the steady state parameters of voltage and current. There is a need for a more reliable operation of system. Gas Insulated Substations have been developed which provide high reliability, consume less space, quick assembly and low maintenance. It is well known that due to switching operations in Gas Insulated Substation (GIS), leads to malfunctioning of substation equipment's. These inappropriate functioning includes misoperation of electronic equipment's, deformation in connected transformer winding and bushing failures. The insulation coordination study thus forms a very important aspect in substation design stage. The dielectric strength of insulation of various connected equipment are effected due to generation very fast transient overvoltage (VFTO), which is caused due to the slow switching operation of disconnector switch in GIS. The objective of this paper is the modeling & analysis of VFTO generation in Gas Insulated Substation and to determine the impact of VFTO on connected equipment. Comparison of different techniques for mitigation of VFTO in GIS are also discussed in the paper. A 400 kV Gas Insulated Substation has been modeled and analyzed using EMTP software.

articleTitle: Improved Integrated Impedance Scheme for Series Compensated Transmission Line
abstract: The paper presents an improved protection scheme for series compensated transmission line. The proposed relaying scheme is based on integrated impedance which is defined as the ratio of the sum of voltage phasors to the current phasors from two ends of a transmission line. The literature shows that the integrated impedance based protection scheme serves as a better option than the conventional current differential protection. However, line-charging current causes significant error in integrated impedance method as well as in conventional current differential method. This paper presents improved integrated impedance-based protection scheme which compensates line charging current using equivalent π-model of the transmission line. The proposed improved integrated impedance scheme is developed in phase domain. The proposed scheme is compared with the integrated impedance and conventional current differential methods. Simulations are carried out in an Alternate Transient Program (ATP) on a 750 kV transmission line equipped with Thyristor Controlled Series Capacitor (TCSC). Simulation results show the superiority of proposed scheme over existing schemes.

articleTitle: Assessment of Features in Smart Meters to Enhance Consumers Safety
abstract: Smart meter provides the vital real time data to the smart grid and is considered the grid's heart. There are many stakeholders to the smart metering program; Utilities, government agencies, `prosumers', and society in general. But, in our opinion it is the electricity consumers who tend to benefit the most from this. Smart meters are equipped with capable measurement and fast computational engine along with latching relays to connect/disconnect supply to the consumer. In this paper, an additional layer of second line of safety is proposed utilising the existing hardware and adding advanced embedded algorithms for consumer safety against `fire from short circuit' and `electric shock'. Fault detection and disconnection response time data generated in the proof of concept experiment is compared with conventional protection class devices.

Author Keywords: safety against electric shock and short circuit

articleTitle: State Frame of Multi-port DC-DC Converter
abstract: This article presents a four-port DC-DC converter (FOPDC), which incorporates DC grid (DGR) [1]-[4] at its port 1 with existing battery bank (BBA), solar photovoltaic (SPH) system, and isolated DC load (DLO) at its ports 2, 3, and 4, respectively. At first, the article develops the state-space (SSP) model [5] for the FOPDC. The SSP model development involves the small signal modeling of the FOPDC through the large signal analysis of the latter. Afterward, the note compares nonlinear large, and linear small signal time-domain modeling responses for each of the state involved in the SSP model of the FOPDC in the MATLAB/Simulink platform.

articleTitle: PV Fed Active Clamped ZVS High Voltage Gain DC-DC Converter for Grid-Tied Photovoltaic Applications
abstract: Owing to the large power demand, the grid-tied PV systems have turn into a necessary sustainable energy source to minimize the effects of greenhouse gases and environmental impacts. To feed the low output PV modules to the grid a high gain and efficient dc-dc converters are required. A high-gain converter based on the integration of the active clamp circuit with a coupled inductor (CI) is introduced in this paper. This high gain is achieved by utilizing the switched capacitors on the secondary side of CI. The clamp circuit alleviates leakage energy problems which minimize the voltage spikes across the switching devices. Further, the zero-voltage switching (ZVS) state is also achieved for the main as well as auxiliary switch. Finally, a 500W, 100kHz proposed converter is simulated in MATLAB/Simulink with PV input at different irradiation levels.

articleTitle: Optimizing Billing Cost and Revenue in PV - BES Integrated Residential Society
abstract: Developing countries like INDIA mainly depends on conventional sources to meet the energy demand because of cheaper price. To meet the sustainable development goals every country is reducing their carbon footprint, this is possible when the energy generation can be shifted from conventional to renewable. As the energy demand is increasing, to meet the demand the penetration of renewable energy mainly photo voltaic panel (PV) is increasing exponentially on residential and commercial sites as they are eco-friendly in nature. However, the existing power plants are running on fossil fuel which are creating air pollution and burning the fossil fuel in huge amount. In this paper, a mathematical model is proposed of residential buildings which are integrated with PV and Battery Energy Storage (BES). Proposed model is a problem with maximizing the revenue from BES and minimizing the electricity bill of residential buildings in 2 different modes of operation. As indicated by the results, the electricity bill is reduced by using BES and PV.

articleTitle: Multi-objective residential demand side management with solar and wind energy integration
abstract: This paper introduces an optimal household demand side management (DSM) program with the integration of inhouse renewable energy resources (RERs). With the help of a smart battery energy storage system (BESS), the utilization of RER integration is maximized in this paper. The minimization of peak load demand and the minimization of every consumer's energy bill are chosen as objectives of this DSM program. Generally, smart residential users are equipped with different controllable appliances which have complex constraints too. Therefore, an evolutionary method is used to solve the proposed residential DSM model. Additionally, the popular economic tool which is the cash payback period (CPP) has also been applied in this paper to investigate the initial investment benefits of RERs and BESS. Six distinct scenarios have been demonstrated in this paper to evaluate the performance of proposed residential DSM model.

articleTitle: Adaptive Voltage Based Relay Setting for PV Connected Distribution System
abstract: Inverter based distributed generations (IBDGs) have gained popularity in order to reduce carbon emission from fossil fuel based power plants. The contribution of very low fault currents due to low thermal overload capability and low voltage ride through (LVRT) techniques applied to control the voltage has resulted in different voltage profile than the fault condition with conventional synchronous machines. As a result, integration of these sources in distribution grid has caused maloperation of conventional over current relays (OCRs). In this paper, the adaptive setting of the OCR has been proposed using estimated voltage considering the operation of LVRT. The validation of the method proposed is been investigated on an IEEE distribution system comprising of 12 buses, using DIgSILENT Power Factory 2018 software and results obtained are significantly better. Both the time of operation of relays is improved and coordination is maintained.

articleTitle: MRZA-LMM with IMTOGI Control for Grid Tied PV System
abstract: This paper deals with a power quality improvement through MRZA-LMM (Modified Reweighted Zero-Attracting Least Mean M-estimate) with IMTOGI (Improved Mixed Third-Order Generalized Integrator) based control algorithm for a grid tied PV (Photovoltaic) system. The proposed control technique is used to control the PV panel power and to deliver the good quality at the utility distribution grid. The proposed control strategy is divided into two parts (1) extraction of fundamental weight component from the distorted load current and (2) extracting the unit template from the unbalanced and distorted grid voltage. The first objective is achieved through proposed MRZA-LMM control. It has fast convergence speed with low steady state errors. The prime objective of the control is met by the IMTOGI technique to estimate the balanced and sinusoidal grid synchronizing signals. This good quality of grid synchronizing signals are helpful to connect the AC/DC converter to the grid and injects the solar DC power into the main grid. The proposed control algorithm is through experimental results at steady state and transient conditions.

articleTitle: Multilevel Inverter Topology with Symmetrical and Asymmetrical Sources for Distributed Energy Resources
abstract: In this research paper, a 1-φ multi-level inverter configuration with the decreased number of switching components is recommended for distributed energy resource applications. The planned inverter able to generate seven and nine output voltage levels with symmetrical and asymmetrical source configuration. Due to the decreased number of semiconductor switches the topology has low power loss compared to conventional 7-level inverter. The developed topology has reliable operation in case of switch failure. The developed topology is simulated with the assistance of Matlab/Simulink software.

articleTitle: Multi-Attacking Strategy on Smart Grid with Incomplete Network Information
abstract: The chances of cyber-attacks have been increased because of incorporation of communication networks and information technology in power system. Main objective of the paper is to prove that attacker can launch the attack vector without the knowledge of complete network information and the injected false data can't be detected by power system operator. This paper also deals with analyzing the impact of multi-attacking strategy on the power system. This false data attacks incurs lot of damage to power system, as it misguides the power system operator. Here, we demonstrate the construction of attack vector and later we have demonstrated multiple attacking regions in IEEE 14 bus system. Impact of attack vector on the power system can be observed and it is proved that the attack cannot be detected by power system operator with the help of residue check method.

articleTitle: Investigation of Influence of Derived Weather Variables using two different Approaches for Modeling Day-Ahead Hourly Electric Load Power Demand Forecasting Framework with Standard Long Short-Term Memory Networks
abstract: Electric Load Power Demand Forecasting (ELPDF) is a key activity in power system operation and control networks. This helps to make consumer friendly and efficient distribution network. With the integration of renewable energy sources and adaptation of various demand side response strategies, a most accurate short-term prediction of electrical load power consumption is mandatory. The proposed day-ahead ELPDF models are created on a new parallel multiple inputs and output framework using two different approaches with chosen features as per empirical knowledge obtained through continuous research. The models are developed in standard LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) network using deep learning techniques. The statistical errors used for evaluating the performance of ELPDF are presented herewith. Irrespective of variations in weather and consumer behavior, the models proposed here yields an average forecast error of 2.8% to 3.6% for day-ahead ELPDF. Also, these models are easier to implement and individually produces the very near forecast at an accuracy of 96.4%.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fault Location Algorithm for Series Compensated Line Using Relay data
abstract: Conventional fault location techniques has limited performance when the fault loop includes Metal Oxide varistor protected series capacitor due to its different operating modes. However, the distance up to fault point form relay location is important while quick restore of the power is considered and this is demanded by the consumers. A single end data based new fault location algorithm is recommended to compute the fault distance accurately in series compensated line. Using the power factor angle and time constant during fault at relay end, it is concluded that fault loop includes series compensation or not. When fault occurs after the series capacitor, to detect the Metal oxide varistor (MOV) operation change in power factor angle is considered and the fault location estimation algorithm is modified accordingly on the basis of the variation in equivalent impedance offered by MOV. The fault location algorithm is evaluated on 400KV two bus system has the length of 300km, series compensated transmission line by using MATLAB/ SIMULINK platform. It is validating for changing the levels of compensation in the middle of the transmission line and also by varying the fault location found to be efficient and accurate.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Performance Analysis of TiO2 based Photo Electro Chemical Cell
abstract: The photo electro chemical (PEC) cell involves a chemical reaction of water, titanium dioxide (TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) and silver nano particles. The TiO2 used in this paper, acts as a photo catalyst and silver nano particles (AgNP) enhances the conductivity. Along with the aforesaid, carbon particles have been used as light absorber and the electrodes act as charge collectors. The PEC fabricated in this work is capable of producing free hydrogen, thus, enhancing the hydrogen economy. Among all the procedures for hydrogen generation, PEC is the most efficient process. For both normal electrolysis and brown gas generator (HHO) kit, external electricity requirement is the main constraint. But in PEC process there is no need of external electricity for hydrogen generation. For the fabrication of PEC, a container has been used to mix water, TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, silver nano particles and carbon particles. After setting up of the experimental setup, the model has been tested for both dark and bright conditions. The simulations and outdoor experiments have been done using PEC model of 20gm TiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> in 200ml of water, under Standard Test Conditions. Simulations were carried out in CHEMCAD version 7 to obtain the output hydrogen and output oxygen. According to the simulation results, the amount of volume of hydrogen and oxygen output are 0.6206 moles and 0.3103 moles respectively. Due to the low efficiency of power generation by the PEC system, the widespread use of PEC has not been possible on a regular basis. The negative effect of corrosion on the whole process has been depicted experimentally in this paper and an alternative has also been proposed. The electrolysis process has been tested with both Potassium hydroxide (KOH) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) as electrolyte separately with the water. From the results, it is observed that KOH is better for generation of HHO gas.

articleTitle: Relative Stability Analysis of Load Frequency Control with QRAWCP-PID controller
abstract: In this paper, the relative stability analysis of perturbed single area non-reheated turbine load frequency model with a PID controller tuned via quadratic regulator approach with compensating pole (QRAWCP) is presented. The analysis is carried out using Routh criterion for variations in governor speed regulation of a single area Non-reheated turbine system for the designed controller. Further, the analysis is compared for existing control methods with load disturbances and parametric uncertainties by integral error performance indices.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Smoothening Application of BESS for Large Solar Photovoltaic Parks
abstract: In this paper, a Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) based solution has been proposed to reduce the fluctuations in the output power of large solar Photovoltaic (PV) parks. This will contribute to reduction in the frequency deviations of large power systems and moderating pressure on conventional power plants with the increasing penetration of solar power. Solar PV smoothening is one such application of BESS to moderate inherent intermittencies of solar PV power plants. Different methods adopted for smoothening of solar PV output could lead to arrival of different sizes of the batteries. Thus, assessment of various methods to smoothen PV output power and scope of smoothening becomes significant. A technique has been proposed and has been evaluated against different existing methods for comparing the performance. The results from the proposed technique have been found to be encouraging in terms of determining the battery life and size.

articleTitle: SSB-CPSO Based Multi-Objective Security Constrained Unit Commitment Solution Using NBI
abstract: Over the past few years, there has been a tremendous rise in energy demand owing to ever increasing urbanization and industrialization. This is evident from the rapid exhaustion of the available fossil fuels and numerous environmental hazards. This paper is an attempt to highlight the trade-off obtained between the minimization of cost and emission by implementing Normal Boundary Intersection (NBI) technique. The paper solves Security Constrained Unit Commitment(SCUC) with and without contingencies employing Search Space Based Crazy Particle Swarm Optimization (SSB-CPSO) algorithm. The efficacy of the proposed methodology has been tested on IEEE-118 bus system in MATLAB. The numerical results thus obtained reveal the efficiency of the algorithm by virtue of the near-optimal solutions that this technique yields.

articleTitle: Micro Hydropower in Nepal: A Journey from Stand-alone System to Distributed Generation
abstract: Nepal is known for its successful rural electrification efforts through community owned and managed standalone micro hydropower projects (MHP) that have helped transform its rural economy. Unfortunately, as soon as the national grid reaches a micro hydro catchment area, things start falling apart. For various reasons, people's preference is the grid and eventually switch over from MHP which then lies idle and ultimately abandoned. A recent survey carried out by the Alternative Energy Promotion Centre (AEPC) shows that about 8% of the MHPs in Province 1 have shut down. The number of abandoned plant would be much larger if MHPs of less than 10kW capacity are also considered. Thus, the Government of Nepal came-up with the policy for grid interconnection of MHPs of less than 100kW capacity. This opportunity of transforming a standalone system to grid connected system has several advantages for both the utility grid and the MHP, the grid gets power injection near the load centers whereas MHP earns additional revenue. The technological difference between grid interconnection of MHP and other hydropower projects shall be discussed in detail in the Nepalese context. A MATLAB simulation analysis is presented to demonstrate the technical viability of the interconnection in the 11kV feeder line. Moreover, financial and economic analysis of the grid interconnected systems is also discussed. This paper also focuses on how droop features of Electronic Load Controller (ELC) could have managed the proportional load sharing among the MHP plants if such ELC with droop features were available.

articleTitle: Coordinated control of HESS in Wind power systems
abstract: Energy storage systems contribute to improving power quality of systems which have large penetration of renewable sources. This paper discusses the use of a hybrid storage system that can be controlled to work in coordination with a small capacity wind farm. Their control has been designed in such a manner as to reduce the cycling of one device and increase its life span when used to smoothen the power output of a wind farm. A flywheel and battery based hybrid system is studied where the battery charges or discharges as required with lower frequency profile as compared to the flywheel. Frequency based methods are used to find the cut-off frequency which determines the power reference fluctuations of each device. Results show that power smoothing is possible and therefore wind power systems can be made to behave as conventional generators. The work has been done in DIgSILENT PowerFactory.

articleTitle: A Cost Frontier Model for Indian Electricity Generating Utilities: A Stochastic Approach
abstract: An econometric cost frontier model is applied to a sample of 30 electricity generating utilities operating in India for the panel data of 4 years from 2010-11 to 2013-14. The objective of this study is to contribute to a deeper understanding of which factors influence cost inefficiency in electricity generation. The results show significant opportunities for cost reduction in the generation industry that could result in price reductions to electricity consumers.

articleTitle: Impact of Demand Response in Integartion of Renewable Energy Resources in Smart Grid
abstract: Nowadays, due to modernization in technology and need of bulk power, impact of demand response (DR) in integration of renewable resources in a smart grid (SG) plays a major part in the development of society. In this study, the impact of DR is investigated in integrated renewable resources in SG. Due to intermittency in renewable resources it is modeled as a stochastic process. A hybrid power system is considered in this study consisting of integrated power generation from thermal, wind turbine and photovoltaic system. Controller parameters in this study are tuned with proportional integration (PI) based particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm. Simulation results and analysis are obtained for studied system, which illustrate the effectiveness of proposed method for studied system.

articleTitle: Analysis and Control of Quasi Z-source Inverter with Digital Current Control for Energy Storage
abstract: The impedance source-based inverter has several advantages in the field of Photovoltaic (PV) systems. It overcomes several drawbacks of conventional PV systems because of its capability to invert and boost the available input voltage through a single power conversion stage. The paper focuses on a quasi-impedance source topology which has several advantages over traditional PV inverter and other traditional impedance source inverters. Application of energy storage to such a topology makes it more suitable for both standalone and grid applications. Thus the paper includes energy storage single-phase impedance source inverter for a standalone PV application with the key elements such as feed-forward MPPT control, output voltage control and a new implementation of digital current control for the bi-directional converter which operates on the available intermittent nature of the PV power. Thus this paper includes a detail numerical and operational analysis of the topology and the control mentioned above, followed by simulation and hardware verification of the above configuration.

articleTitle: Transmission Expansion Planning in Deregulated Electricity Markets using Multi-Criteria Data Envelopment Analysis (MCDEA)
abstract: This paper presents an effective method for transmission expansion planning (TEP) in a pool-based competitive electricity market. For this, a social welfare function (SWF) is maximized for the nonlinear optimization problem of TEP, subject to security and power flow operational constraints. The social welfare function compromises the benefit of consumers and real power generation costs. The adaptable candidate lines are obtained fit for several perspective scenarios of future demand. Later, the objective function of the formulated problem compared with the annual investment cost of the forthcoming transmission line. The relative performance of each available line is assessed by the application of Multi-criteria Data Envelopment Analysis (MCDEA) and considers the most efficient adaptable line for the TEP. The proposed method is tested on Garver's six-bus system to demonstrate the expansion study.

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage System Operational Control for Distribution Transformer Overload Management
abstract: A distribution transformer is an important asset whose failure causes huge financial loss to a utility and scarcity of power for end consumers. One of the prime causes for failure of Distribution Transformers (DTs) is overloading. A Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) can reduce the stress on a DT by discharging itself during peak demand periods. An effective energy management methodology for BESS at DT level has been presented in this paper. A novel method for battery charging & discharging is proposed based on real-time net power flow measurements from DT and from load-side, considering penetration of rooftop solar Photovoltaic (PV) power at consumer end. BESS will be charged and discharged during off peak and peak demand periods respectively. The designed BESS has a bi-directional converter and solar PV with boost converter that are connected at the DC-link of their respective individual three-phase converters. The control logic for battery charging/discharging is developed in such a way that the power flow from distribution transformer shall not exceed 80 % of its rated capacity. The charging is performed under two modes of operation. Current control mode charging is preferred till battery SoC is 80%. Subsequently, voltage control mode of charging is performed up to 95% SoC level. The modeling and simulation is carried out in MATLAB<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> and results are presented to showcase the effectiveness of proposed control logic for different modes of operation. The proposed methodology will be tested and validated on real-time HIL testing platform for pre-pilot implementation validation.

articleTitle: Implementation of Ultra-Wide Band Marx Generator with Improvised PFN Topology for Antenna Load
abstract: Impulse waveforms have similar characteristics as that of lightning strike and are used for a wide range of applications. This paper is regarding a Marx Generator merged with pulse forming network (PFN) along with improvisation of Marx using boosting technique. Solid state switches undergo periodic switching to enable charging-discharging cycles of inductors and capacitors. Result of five-staged model simulation in MATLAB/Simulink for an input of 20kV is a 250kV, 150ns pulse to match the output of a high frequency (HF) radio antenna load. A dummy load of 50ohms is connected for testing purpose which is same as the impedance of the antenna or transmission line that is used with the transmitter. A hardware prototype is also designed and assembled to verify the simulation results.

articleTitle: Restoration in Microgrid using System Stability Criteria
abstract: In a complex power system network; faults are inevitable in nature. They can only be cleared after their occurrence using various protection devices. When the faults are cleared and the faulty sections are isolated, restoration of the system should be done as soon as possible so that end-users get power supply with no further delay. Restoration of the network is a very challenging task as it involves synchronization of many system parameters and also all the system security constraints must be satisfied during the restoration phase. Keeping these aspects into consideration, a multi-agent-based approach is proposed for power system restoration. The technique is applied to a 7-bus microgrid system to validate the proposed restoration scheme.

articleTitle: Frequency Separation in Mixed Inertia Power Systems Using Modular Approach
abstract: We show that synchronous generators in power systems have their own characteristic frequencies which depend on topology and parameters of network. This revelation leads to a new method of dynamic analysis of power systems. A weighted mix of characteristic frequencies constitutes a consensus - the average system frequency. Consensus implies only an estimate in dynamic state since periodic time of waveform varies from cycle to cycle. Increasing frequency separation is an indicator of system's decline towards collapse of synchronous operation. Numerical determination of frequency separation with conventional methods is not straightforward. With modular approach, it is much easier. Coherent generator-clusters can also be detected. Difficulties crop up when sources have low or no inertia. Preferred way to analyze such systems is to use modular approach. We extend steady state modular approach to analyze dynamic aspects of power systems by re-writing module in terms of frequency. Illustrative examples for high and low inertia energy systems are given. Analysis is expected to be useful for design, planning and operation of low inertia power systems.

articleTitle: Determination of the component sizes and analysis of the operational cost of PEM Fuel Cell-Battery Hybrid Energy System to Retrofit the Diesel Locomotives of Indian Railway
abstract: The paper presents a multi-objective design optimization approach for determination of the component sizes of a polymer electrolyte membrane fuel cell (PEMFC)-battery hybrid energy system (HES) to substitute the three diesel locomotive classes operating in Indian railways. The objective functions of optimization are the minimization of the total cost of the HES and the fuel consumption. An energy management strategy is used for the load distribution between the two energy sources and is implemented as the sub-routine in the optimization algorithm. For simulation study, the real-world drive cycle of a local passenger train functional in Assam, India is considered. Three different Pareto fronts containing the different sets of PEMFC and battery sizes are obtained for the three locomotives. Lastly, a comparison between the diesel locomotives and the proposed HES is carried out in terms of their operational cost to examine the advantages of the proposed HES.

articleTitle: Effect of Tower Footing Resistance on Back Flashover for A Double Circuit Line
abstract: An investigation is carried out on an EMTP model of a 400kV double circuit line to analyze overvoltages that occur due to a lightning strike on the phase and the ground wire. Lightning strike response corresponding to different front time and the tower footing resistance are analyzed. In this paper, the impact of back-flashover on the overvoltage profile at different points on the tower is also analyzed. It is observed that both tower footing resistance and front-time of lightning surge play a significant role in determining the value of over-voltage.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Operation with Dispatchable Distributed Generation considering Load Variations
abstract: This paper presents the distribution network operation with distributed generations (DG) considering hourly load variations. The proposed methodology is aimed at handling the hourly load variations effectively by dividing the load demand curve into four different fuzzy load categories and a single DG power output value is obtained at each of these categories. Emphasis is laid on the fact that a single DG power output value can be obtained for all the load levels, on the load demand curve, lying within a particular fuzzy load category. In this work, a fuzzy based approach is used to obtain a single value of load point for each fuzzy load category to handle the load variations. The DG power output is optimized at this load point using genetic algorithm (GA) optimization technique. The objective function defined for optimization is aimed at power loss reduction and voltage profile improvement. The optimum location for DG unit placement is obtained using a stability index based on voltage. Effectiveness of the proposed methodology is demonstrated with the help of a 33 node distribution network.

articleTitle: Accelerated Zone-2 Protection Scheme for Transmission Lines using Traveling Waves
abstract: The acceleration of zone-2 distance protection scheme typically depend on the use of a communication channel. Communication based zone-2 protection scheme may not be feasible in case of degradation or failure of communication channel. This paper presents an accelerated distance relay zone-2 protection scheme using traveling wave arrival time information available at local terminal. Acceleration of distance protection zone-2 is done by using the information of faulted line. Faulted line is identified using first three arrival times traveling waves recorded at local terminal. The proposed technique is tested with PSCAD/EMTDC simulations with different fault types, fault resistances, and locations. The performance study confirms that the technique accurately identifies the faulted zone. This method is used as accelerated zone-2 distance protection scheme for EHV transmission lines when the communication link is failed or not available.

articleTitle: A Study On Effect of Different Control Strategies on Q-f Droop Islanding Detection Technique
abstract: An investigation on the effect of various control strategies on Q-f droop based islanding detection technique (IDT) is presented. The IDT operates by increasing or decreasing the frequency beyond the set limits by injecting reactive power into the system. The technique is proposed for constant real-reactive power inverter control. The effect of control strategies like constant current (CC), constant Power-voltage (PV) control are not studied so far. In this paper the effect of various control strategies on Q-f droop based islanding scheme is analyzed. The Simulations are performed in RTDS/RSCAD domain on a UL1741 standard test system.

articleTitle: Investigation of Passivity Behavior of Synchronous Generators Connected to Passive Network
abstract: Recent advancements in power electronics, storage and renewable technologies have led to a proliferation of distributed energy resources. While the emergence of distributed energy resources provides improved control over the grid, it becomes necessary to analyze the stability of these devices in grid connected mode. It is desirable to provide a simple, robust stability criterion that can be checked locally, without the information of the entire grid. Passivity based stability criterion is well-suited for this purpose as the electrical transmission and distribution network to which these devices are connected is primarily made up of passive components. It is necessary to examine the passivity behavior of synchronous generators, which comprise a large part of the generation in modern grids. This paper presents the passivity behavior of a synchronous machine and the effect of its closed loop controllers on the passivity behavior. It has been observed that the non-passivity can be minimized if the controllers are tuned properly, but the generator is not passive over the entire frequency range. However, it has been observed that passivity can be achieved by encapsulating the generator with a portion of the passive network. Case studies have been carried out using detailed models of the synchronous generators and their controllers.

articleTitle: “Impact of EV on Integration with Grid System – A Review”
abstract: The shortage of fossil fuels and environmental pollution creates pressure for transportation and power system. The use of Electric Vehicle (EVs) can able to mitigate these problems to some extent. Peak load in distribution system can be reduced by using EVs. By using different charging strategies of EV, we can reduce the adverse effect of EV penetration in the peak load demand and hence improves load factor of system. A vehicle with the ability of V2G technology, presents many advantages like filtering of current harmonics, active power regulation, balancing of load etc. With these attributes, EVs provide various ancillary services like spinning reserve and regulation of frequency and voltage. Despite of reducing many challenges in grid system, increased use of EV has come with some other problems for power system. Use of EVs affects the power quality in adverse manner because to recharge their batteries, they required large amount of power. Rising interference of EV in grid causes decrease in life cycle of the transformer. The mining of lithium (which is used in batteries of EV) result in production of greenhouse gases, environmental pollution and affects the human health. This paper presents a detailed review on the impacts of electric vehicle on integration with grid system.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement of Electric Vehicle Charging Stations in a Distribution Network
abstract: The rising popularity and improved environmental awareness are making the present transportation network move towards electric vehicles (EVs). With the increased number of grid-connected EVs, inappropriate placement of charging stations (CSs) will be injurious to city traffic layout and the power distribution network. It will also deprive the convenience of EV owners and increase distribution loss. Therefore, this paper proposes a new method for optimal allocation of CSs by minimizing distribution losses of the system and increasing the utilization factor of CSs. Since these two objectives are contradictory, non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGAII) is used to solve them. A probabilistic load modelling method is employed to develop the charging demand of EVs. The proposed method is tested on a test system which is obtained by modifying the standard IEEE 33 bus system. Simulation results show that the proposed method is not only able to reduce the system loss but also achieve economical benefits while placing CSs in a network.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in Harmonic Resonance Detection in Low Voltage Networks using Impedance Measurement Techniques
abstract: Harmonic resonance is a modern-age power quality issue. These issues are observed in public Low Voltage networks caused by increased penetration of diverse power electronic equipment using grid-side filter circuits and shunt capacitances. Harmonic resonance could result in stability issues or amplified harmonic levels in the network. The paper presents simulation results to emphasize on the importance on harmonic resonance. Further, the paper also provides a comprehensive survey on network harmonic impedance measurement techniques with their application towards harmonic resonance detection.

articleTitle: Assessment of Decentralized Reactive Power Control Strategies for Low Voltage PV Inverters
abstract: The increase of solar PV installations at the distribution grid level causes new challenges that Distribution System Operators have to resolve. Amongst those challenges, one is the voltage fluctuation at the distribution grid level due to intermittent active power injection from solar PV systems. A well-known solution to regulate the voltage is the local consumption or production of reactive power, that is extensively used at the transmission grid level by generators or Flexible AC Transmission Systems. This paper discusses the impacts of low-voltage control by reactive power injection from commercialized rooftop PV solar inverters. Using a fully decentralized approach, several state of the art strategies for PV inverters’ power factor control are compared, showing that some of these decentralized strategies are a viable solution to control voltage in distribution grids. The methodology used for the assessment of these control strategies includes the impact on the inverters’ life time (measured as the annual cost for each strategy) as well as the impact on the voltage profiles of a real grid representing an Indian community with more than 200 households.

articleTitle: Optimal Load Scheduling for Industrial Load - Analysis for a Generalized Industrial Load Model
abstract: The purpose of Demand Response (DR) is to guarantee that the smart grid runs in an efficient and stable way by letting the consumers participate in the grid operation. Numerous studies of DR modeling and analysis are implemented for consumers in the residential and commercial sector, while the studies on DR in industrial sector are relatively immature. In this work, optimal load control for industrial sector is investigated, which involves several new and distinct research problems. For example, while most of residential loads operate independently, industrial units are highly interdependent and must follow certain operational sequences. A generalized industrial load model is proposed here which can be utilized for implementing different types of industries by some simple modification in the model. An integrated framework is designed to find the optimal load schedule for any industry. This framework will help the industrial user in DSM to reduce their expenditure on electrical energy usage and also will give optimal scheduling of the units corresponding to different utility pricing schemes.

articleTitle: Identifying the Potential for Peer-to-Peer Trading of Rooftop Solar Power for Indian Scenario
abstract: Due to the efficacious and continual development in the integration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) with the power grid, the power system is metamorphosing towards a dynamic, decentralized and distributed energy paradigm. DERs are classified as wind turbine generators, rooftop solar PV plants, energy storage devices, and electric vehicles that are usually owned and operated by the end-users of a distribution network. A smart grid framework which incentivizes the active involvement of such end-user based DERs into the grid is the ideal requirement to embrace this transition. Since the end-users not only consume but also generate power as well, for such `Prosumers', Peer to Peer (P2P) trading will provide a market place for localized energy trading between peers, enabling sustainability and ensuring locally balanced distributed energy within the community. This paper proposes an innovative market mechanism and a pricing strategy for the smart grid - "P2P Trading, which allows for each peer of the network to participate in energy trading with each other and with the grid. The paper also shows the potential of P2P trading in reducing consumer costs, and by exploring opportunities for earning revenue for the prosumers from surplus energy. The import and export profiles of a group of consumers of an actual distribution utility have been used for this study. After observing the power profiles of the consumers, the best suitable period for P2P trading has been identified and a possible pricing strategy has been discussed.

articleTitle: Fault Classification in VSC-HVDC Transmission System using Machine Learning Approach
abstract: Transmission system nowadays a complex network due to interconnection with the nearby system for fulfilling high load demand. Therefore, protection of transmission system is also much important. As, protection of transmission system is much complex problem due to less known approaches. HVDC transmission is also at present time important part of transmission line. Therefore, the protection of HVDC system several protection scheme specifically for fault classification are used. This paper presents the use of support vector machine (SVM) based classification approach for Fault estimation in HVDC transmission system. SVM based method is comparatively a novel method that is based on computational as well as theory of statistical learning. Along with the input space vector is made into a dot product of high dimension that is called a feature space in SVM theory. Therefore, the optimal hyper-plane has to be consider greater ability of classification in the feature space. Thus the optimal hyper-plane is to be determined by exploring the theory of optimization, and the critical information providing via the theory of statistical learning. Therefore, SVM approach has got the ability to counter a large featured space vector. So that the proposed approach has ability to assist in the area of fault classification as there is no restriction on the number of features.
